text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate observed from API ingress ELBs in us-west-2a/2b (avg 12% over 2m) — elevated latency and failed health checks on several targets. Related metric: elb_target_5xx_count.

jess: @here I'm paged for us-west-2 ELB 5xx spike, seeing customer reports. taking lead.

marco: on my way. do we know if it's regional or AZ-only? dashboards show spikes in 2a and 2b, 2c looks lower.

priya: routing graphs show a surge of ConnectionAbort errors from NAT gateway ENIs in 2a leading to backend connection resets. Could be cross-AZ egress issue.

arun: 1) ELB health checks are failing to backend HTTP endpoints (503/502) 2) host-level metrics show EBS write latency increased on some nodes in 2a.

jess: ok triage hypothesis: ENI/NAT egress problems in 2a causing backend instances in 2a to fail checks; 2b might be partially affected. Immediate mitigation options: mark 2a targets drained, fail traffic to 2c & us-west-1, rotate Route53 traffic?

maya: declare Sev2 for now, customers experiencing degraded writes and higher error rates. notify CS.

incident-bot: Incident declared: SEV2 — us-west-2 ELB/egress instability impacting API write paths. Pagers: @jess (lead), @marco (sre), escalation in 8m if not acknowledged.

liz: CS watching tickets, a handful of enterprise customers seeing timeouts. prepping status update for status.redwood.ai.

marco: quick check: can we remove 2a targets from ELB target groups to stop repeated retries?

jess: yes if we can drain gracefully. Marco, can you run the drain and shift traffic to 2c + fallback region? keep TTL low on Route53 for quick recovery.

marco: doing. command I'm running: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-api/abcd1234 --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h --region us-west-2``` will iterate across affected target IDs.

priya: also reducing Route53 primary policy weight for us-west-2 to 10% and increasing us-west-1 to handle overflow. plan: update traffic policy, not full failover yet.

arun: note: some autoscaling groups are already replacing instances due to EBS latency. we'll hold scaling until we confirm root.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline paused for us-west-2 due to ongoing incident (auto-pause rule).

marco: deregistered most 2a targets. monitoring shows 5xx dropping from 12% -> 4% over last 60s. good sign.

jess: awesome. @priya keep adjusting Route53 routing. set health check TTL lower, shorten failure threshold.

priya: applied change: Route53 traffic policy updated. Health check interval set to 10s and failure threshold 2. Weight adjusted: us-west-2 20% -> 10%, us-west-1 -> +30%.

incident-bot: Note: Route53 change history: change-id Z3ABCDEFG12345 applied.

marco: continuing to monitor. still seeing intermittent spikes from 2b, might be spillover due to cross-AZ network paths congested.

arun: digging into instance-level logs, seeing many ECONNRESET and socket timeouts on outbound calls to external dependencies (third-party payments). not purely ELB.

jess: need to communicate impact clearly: read-only operations are mostly OK, writes have ~20-40s retries and some failures. CS please post initial status: partial outage for writes in us-west-2.

liz: posting now: "We are investigating increased API errors and timeouts for write operations in the US-West (Oregon) region. Our engineering team is actively mitigating; we will update every 15 minutes." :warning:

maya: handoff plan — @marco will run primary ops for the next 30m, @jess will coordinate with product and execs, I'll keep watch on escalation.

marco: running health check creation for an alternate NLB in us-west-2c to absorb traffic: ```aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-api/zzzz9999 --targets Id=i-0c9d8e7f6g5h4i3j --region us-west-2```

priya: AWS support ticket opened (case 9876543210) — we requested an internal networking check on NAT gateways and ENI error rates in us-west-2a/2b. ETA 20-40m.

jess: good. also remind: we can't do broad DB failover to us-west-1 yet — riskier. prefer routing new requests to healthy instances while we remediate.

marco: 15m update: 5xx now 1.8% sustained. traffic shift to us-west-1 and us-west-2c holding. AWS support says they're seeing elevated host-level packet drops in AZ 2a; their engineers continuing investigation.

incident-bot: Reminder: create runbook entry for this incident and capture all commands/changes for postmortem.

jess: agreed. Marco — please capture exact target IDs and Route53 change-ids in the runbook. Priya, capture AWS support updates. Liz, publish 15m status update noting partial recovery and ongoing investigation.

liz: status update posted. customers asking about SLA credits — will coordinate with legal/finance once root cause confirmed.

maya: After-action item flagged: improve auto-evacuation playbook for AZ-level ENI/NAT outages and add a DR test for Route53 weighted failover.

arun: one more note: we saw node-level EBS high write latency correlate with AZ symptoms — possible EBS control plane degradation in 2a. AWS acknowledged increased EBS latencies in their internal note.

marco: handing primary ops to @maya at 1876501500 — I'll remain available for runbook cleanup.

maya: taking over. Tracker updated. continuing watch. last check: error rate stable at ~0.8%.

jess: thanks team. we'll keep status updates until AWS confirms root cause. postmortem lead: @marco.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (traffic shifted, targets drained, monitoring stable). Will remain open pending AWS postmortem and internal RCA.

liz: posted final initial update to status page: mitigated, investigation ongoing. customers notified.

marco: capturing all logs and commands into incident runbook: https://phabricator.internal/INC-1876501234 (added links to CloudTrail, ELB logs, Route53 change history).

jess: bravo team. we'll reconvene in 24h for RCA and timelines for DR improvements. :thumbsup:
